message.content: {"recommended_method":"social_choice","consensus_potential":0.68,"fairness_assessment":"A ranked or score-based vote fairly compares the three budget allocations, avoids letting the debate winner determine the outcome alone, and allows participants to express support for a balanced compromise. Fairness would improve if costs, recruitment evidence, equipment condition, and measurable outcomes were documented before voting.","conflict_severity":"medium","stakeholder_analysis":[{"agent":"Agent A","position":"Supports using the full budget for an inter-city tournament with catering and prizes to increase club visibility and recruit members.","influence":0.72},{"agent":"Agent B","position":"Supports investing the full budget in educational equipment, especially replacing worn chessboards, clocks, and teaching materials.","influence":0.86},{"agent":"Agent C","position":"Supports splitting the budget evenly between a smaller tournament and educational equipment to balance visibility and pedagogy.","influence":0.76}],"recommended_resolution":"compromise","governance_reasoning":"The three options represent legitimate but competing objectives: outreach, instructional quality, and balance. Social choice is appropriate because the alternatives can be ranked or scored transparently, while a compromise resolution is likely to preserve broader support. A conditional or staged allocation could improve the compromise by funding essential equipment first and reserving the remainder for a tournament tied to explicit recruitment and visibility targets."}
